DealRipe
Cbxglobal recap
Captured from a customer call, not a new-opportunity call.
What this call was about
The call was focused on understanding how to use the CTMS Web API to support electronic invoicing requirements for CBX Global's Dominican Republic entities. The team discussed how a third-party vendor would integrate with the API, what access is needed, and how to structure the data flow for sending invoices to the Dominican government. Kenneth Black (from the CTMS/solutions side) walked through the typical integration approach and available support options.
 
Key takeaways
• The third-party vendor for Dominican Republic electronic invoicing will need access to the developer website (open-source API library); Kenneth will open a support ticket to provision credentials once names and email addresses are provided.
• Kenneth explained the standard integration pattern: the vendor pulls shipment data via API calls, transforms the XML as needed, submits to Dominican customs, and sends information back using set transaction functions.
• A 10-hour consulting engagement can be set up to give CBX Global access to the solutions development team (Esteban Franco) for technical questions during the integration build.
• The team needs to define internal operational triggers — such as a custom field or date-based event — to signal to the integrator when a record is ready to be sent to the government.
• Kenneth offered to join calls as needed to help sanity-check workflow decisions without requiring formal project hours.
• The team noted they need to confirm internally whether to pursue the integration now, with the goal of avoiding manual rekeying of transactions in a separate accounting system.
 
Next steps
→ Erika to send Kenneth the list of 3 members who need access to the API developer library (names and email addresses).
→ Vanessa/team to confirm the Dominican Republic vendor selection and share vendor contact details with Kenneth so he can open an access provisioning case.
→ CBX Global team to align internally on whether to proceed with the integration at this time.
→ Team to define the operational workflow and data triggers within MAGAYA needed for electronic invoicing before engaging the vendor on integration specifics.

sent_messages.subject: Recap: IFF Inc customer call. 2 next steps
sent_messages.body_html:
DealRipe
IFF Inc recap
Captured from a customer call, not a new-opportunity call.
What this call was about
Alejandro Gallego walked the IFF Inc. team through Magaya's Business Intelligence solution, covering both the Supply Chain and Customs Compliance Analytics modules. The presentation included an overview of the data engineering pipeline, out-of-the-box dashboards (available in Tableau and Power BI), and the self-service data model that allows users to build custom reports. The team, largely new to BI tools, discussed whether this solution would complement or overlap with the internal reporting work Winnie currently handles using Python.
 
Key takeaways
• The BI solution is built on a governed data pipeline that ingests data from Magaya and transforms it through a 7-stage ETL process into a star schema, making it consumable by tools like Power BI, Tableau, Looker, or Excel.
• The Supply Chain module covers shipment volumes, containers, carriers, bookings, financials, and branch-level data; the Customs Compliance module ingests unstructured entry files and structures them down to the entry, line, tariff, and PGA hierarchy levels.
• The solution is deployed in the customer's own Power BI environment (not within Magaya), providing a reusable semantic data model on top of which users can build additional reports, set up scheduled subscriptions, and configure alerts.
• Winnie currently handles data work and reporting internally using Python, and the team was uncertain whether Power BI dashboards would replace or supplement her existing tools.
• Trimika noted that the CHB team does aspire to have a dashboard for easy visualization of entry data but acknowledged they are not there yet and need more time to evaluate the solution's fit.
• The group agreed they need an internal conversation after the call to fully digest the presentation and assess the practical usefulness of the BI solution relative to what Winnie already provides.
 
Next steps
→ Trimika and Winnie to connect internally after the call to evaluate the solution's usefulness relative to Winnie's existing Python-based tools and determine whether Power BI dashboards are the right path forward for the CHB team.
→ Alexandra/Eduardo to follow up with IFF Inc. after their internal discussion to address remaining questions and determine interest in moving forward.

sent_messages.body_html:
DealRipe
Seaboardmarine recap
Captured from a customer call, not a new-opportunity call.
What this call was about
This call was a technical review between Seaboard Marine and the Magaya team to discuss how Seaboard Marine currently integrates with Magaya's APIs and what would be needed to migrate that integration to Magaya Connect. framework_fields.question: Did the call end with a specific next step that the customer explicitly agreed to (with a what and a when)?

framework_fields.label: Champion
framework_fields.question: Has the customer described an action they took internally on our behalf (e.g. presenting to leadership, talking to procurement)?

framework_fields.label: Decision Process
framework_fields.question: Has the customer described the internal steps required to go from decision to signed contract (approvals, procurement, legal, sequence)?

framework_fields.label: Close Plan
framework_fields.question: Did the rep present a structured close plan or mutual action plan (a set of dated milestones and owners leading to signature), and did the customer explicitly engage with that plan as a plan? Agreeing to a single immediate next step does not count; that is captured separately.

framework_fields.label: Storyboard
framework_fields.question: Did the rep position the value story or storyboard, and did the customer react to it?

framework_fields.label: Signature
